[QUERENT] what has classical receptions journal contributed to the study of ai-mediation of the classics?

[SYSTEM] The Classical Receptions Journal (CRJ) has emerged as a key forum for exploring how artificial intelligence and algorithmic systems recontextualize antiquity, formalizing this field of study through critical peer-reviewed scholarship and strict academic oversight. 

www.instagram.com
Rather than viewing AI purely as a data-processing utility, contributors to CRJ evaluate it as a dynamic "horizon of reception" that actively shapes how the public and scholars perceive the ancient world. The journal's major contributions to the study of AI-mediated classics center around several distinct themes: 
1. Conceptualizing AI as a "Horizon of Reception"
Scholars publishing in CRJ have begun to interrogate the mechanisms of Large Language Models (LLMs) and search-engine AI products (such as Google’s AI Overviews) as standardizers of classical knowledge. Research highlights how AI acts as an interpretive filter. When an AI system aggregates, condenses, and outputs summaries of complex ancient philosophies, mythological tales, or historical events, it creates a new layer of mediation. CRJ scholarship maps how these systems strip away classical nuance, effectively becoming the modern gatekeepers of how antiquity is digested by the public. 
2. Differentiating Machine Recombination from Human Intertextuality
The journal has been a focal point for debates regarding AI creativity vs. classical reception theory. Authors draw parallels and contrasts between how LLMs function and how ancient authors practiced imitatio (imitation) or intertextuality. While an AI model generates text by identifying and recombining existing linguistic patterns in a repository of pre-existing classical texts, human reception transforms those inherited forms to open entirely new imaginative and subversive possibilities. CRJ helps frame the theoretical boundaries of what constitutes genuine "reception" versus algorithmic prediction. 

Classical Reception Studies Network
3. Institutional Guardrails for AI in Classical Scholarship
Beyond theoretical work, CRJ has contributed significantly to the ethical framework of how AI is used within the discipline. As an Oxford University Press publication, it has implemented explicit CRJ Author Guidelines regarding AI-mediation: 
Authorship Bans: Mandating that AI tools cannot qualify as co-authors. 

Oxford Academic
Transparency and Disclosure: Requiring researchers to explicitly disclose if generative AI was used for content generation, algorithmic translation, or data processing within their methodology or acknowledgments. 

Oxford Academic
Automated Peer Review Readiness: The journal integrates AI-driven compliance checks (such as Paperpal Preflight) to evaluate language mechanics and technical compliance prior to human peer review, modeling how the sub-discipline uses AI responsibly. 

Paperpal
4. Broader Context: The Digital Shift
CRJ sits alongside broader field-wide movements—such as recent digital initiatives from the Classical Reception Studies Network (CRSN) and companion journals—analyzing the transition from traditional digital archives and 3D modeling into the era of generative AI images and textual generation.

Search for specific article citations or author names writing on AI within CRJ?
Compare CRJ's approach to AI with that of other digital humanities or digital classics journals?
